To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the P22 DNA concatemer is cleaved by a site-specific DNA endonuclease, and the cleaved concatemer is then encapsulated into a preformed head.
P22 head morphogenesis is controlled by the DNA length of the concatemeric intermediate.

1) P22 DNA is cut from concatemer DNA by a mechanism that involves head assembly; 2) the head assembly mechanism is the same in both P22-infected and P22-lysogeny cells; 3) the head assembly protein (P23) is required for the headful cutting mechanism; and 4) the cutting mechanism is not a random process but is directed to specific sites in the concatemer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the bacteriophage P22 and its relatives.
the molecular biology of the phage P22.
understanding the mechanism by which the DNA is packaged into the phage head, and the mechanism of the DNA cutting reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanism of encapsulation of phage DNA is a result of the interaction between the DNA and the phage head proteins, and that this process is intimately connected to and dependent on the morphogenesis of phage heads.
the DNA is encapsulated into the head by a process of cutting of the concatemeric DNA, and the cutting is controlled by the morphogenesis of phage heads.
phage P22 head assembly is a complex, multi-step, multi-protein, energy-requiring, and DNA-dependent process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P22 morphogenesis proceeds in a series of steps, each of which can be blocked by a mutation.
the P22 head is assembled from the inside out, starting with the assembly of a protein scaffold.
the DNA packaging process is a two-step reaction, the first of which is the formation of the concatemeric DNA intermediate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of DNA encapsulation is not a simple process of head filling.
the DNA packaging mechanism in phages like P22 and T7 is very different than in the tailed bacteriophages like lambda and T4.
P22 DNA encapsulation requires a DNA polymerase and a DNA ligase.
